source_title: Asian Champions Trophy 2026: Harmanpreet, Sukhjeet star in India’s 5-2 win over China - Sportstar
source_excerpt: JALANDHAR Coach Craig Fulton had admitted that the Chinese team at the Asian Champions Trophy was unknown and it was difficult to plan against. On Thursday, India found how out how much, clearly the better side but also struggling to find the gaps before prevailing 5-2. After the goalfest against Bangladesh, India was up against a China with a very clear plan – pack the midfield, deny India space on the ground and force it to go in the air, then defend with everything it has. It almost worked, the Indians having to adapt, relying on their experience to find ways not only into the Chinese circle but also to keep the them at bay. A long aerial pass from India’s 25-yard line by Jugraj Singh was brought down just inside the China circle by Sukhjeet Singh, controlled and carried a couple of steps ahead on the stick before unleashing a rasping hit over the head of advancing goalkeeper Huanyu Wu in the 12th minute to open the scoring. To China’s credit, its structure held firm with a counterattack a couple of shots on goal but was unable to score. It finally levelled through Yang Peng’s penalty corner conversion in the 26th minute, only for Mandeep Singh to be checked on a counter and get India a PC of its own, Harmanpreet Singh making no mistake to restore the lead. The big positive was the team’s sustained momentum either side of the break, something Fulton has admitted has been frustratingly lacking. Two goals inside the first five minutes post break made it 4-1, Harmanpreet and Sukhjeet adding one each. Another PC in the 36th minute for China and another goal made it 4-2 before Jugraj Singh got on the scoresheet with a PC of his own. Fulton would also be happy with India’s pace and the fact that not only the aerials were used to good effect but also the Indian midfield’s ability to constantly rotate and stretch the opposition thin to move ahead.
